pubs.ssci-2026-01: Paid subscriptions like Netflix and ad-supported free tiers pull viewers in different directions. Examines how conversation on social media shapes the use of free versus paid streaming services.
pubs.ssci-2026-02: On luxury resale platforms a high price can pull buyers in at one moment and push them away at the next. Identifies the conditions under which price premiums drive demand and those under which they deter it.
pubs.ssci-2026-03: Do people open their apps more on rainy days? Combines the spaces people occupy with the day's weather to explain patterns of mobile app engagement.
pubs.ssci-2026-04: The same push notification lands differently when it feels personal. A field experiment testing whether personalized push notifications actually raise user engagement.
pubs.ssci-2026-05: Notifications that speak with human-like emotion do not work the same way for everyone. Examines how the effect of emotionally anthropomorphized alerts shifts with how often someone uses the app.
pubs.ssci-2025-01: Even anonymous strangers change how much players spend. Draws on real online game data to show how playing alongside unknown others shapes spending.
pubs.ssci-2025-02: Click, sign up, purchase — consumers respond to real-time mobile offers differently at each step. Maps those differences into guidance on when to send which offer.
pubs.ssci-2025-03: A bigger brand logo can promote the post and suppress its sharing at the same time. An empirical look at how logo size in social media posts affects virality.
pubs.ssci-2025-04: In immersive technologies such as VR and AR, is being a foreign firm an asset or a handicap? Analyzes the liability of foreignness in extended reality innovation from an international business perspective.
pubs.ssci-2024-01: “Your card was charged” — even routine payment alerts can change how people spend. Documents the surprising consequences of innocuous mobile transaction reminders for consumer spending.
pubs.ssci-2024-02: A nearby physical store does not lift every product's online sales equally. Shows that the effect of offline store presence on digital sales depends on how functional the product is.
pubs.ssci-2024-03: How older adults pick a healthcare provider is a question aging societies cannot avoid. Examines what older consumers' choices mean amid local competition in healthcare services.
pubs.ssci-2023-01: How much does the fear of a data leak hold technology use back? A meta-analysis synthesizing a large body of prior work on privacy concern and information technology.
pubs.ssci-2023-02: Tastes are not fixed; they keep shifting. Designs a recommendation system that tracks changing preferences and applies it to the mobile game industry.
pubs.ssci-2022-01: Does a handwritten note in the delivery box actually work? A field experiment on how handwritten notes from online retailers affect customer response.
pubs.ssci-2022-02: The emotional tone of a video's thumbnail and title can decide the fate of the ad in front of it. Analyzes how pre-roll advertising effectiveness varies with the emotional tone of the content.
pubs.ssci-2022-03: Time spent on Instagram can carry over into time spent in shopping apps. Traces the link from social media app use to shopping app use on the same smartphone.
pubs.ssci-2022-04: Bad news spreads faster and louder. Uses microblog and news data to document sentiment change and negative herding in public opinion.
pubs.ssci-2022-05: What happens to incumbents once everyday medicines can be sold outside pharmacies? Analyzes incumbent firms' performance and strategic responses to over-the-counter drug deregulation.
pubs.ssci-2021-01: Does living digitally make people happier? Examines the roles of digital-native status and privacy concern in the digital well-being of Asian consumers.
pubs.ssci-2021-02: Shoppers buying electronics often stay in the channel they used before. Compares Korean and Chinese consumer data to analyze channel stickiness along the shopping journey.
pubs.ssci-2021-03: How do small and medium-sized firms find trading partners in online B2B marketplaces? An empirical analysis of buyer–supplier matching on such platforms.
pubs.ssci-2021-04: Who are the shoppers who move freely between stores and online? Profiles multichannel shoppers in the French apparel industry and what retailers can do with them.
pubs.ssci-2020-01: Products bought now and enjoyed later — concert tickets, for instance — sit between the online and offline worlds. Analyzes how both environments drive online social interaction and sales.
pubs.ssci-2020-02: There is a reason online-first brands open physical stores. A ‘clicks to bricks’ study of what happens when digital retailers introduce products in offline stores.
pubs.ssci-2020-03: Do usage limits such as game ‘shutdown laws’ actually work? Evaluates what such laws did to real playing time and spending, adding evidence to the policy debate.
pubs.ssci-2019-01: Earlier reviews can sway the rating the next person leaves. Analyzes TripAdvisor review data to examine how eWOM characteristics affect consumer ratings.
pubs.ssci-2019-02: Can a celebrity endorser lift the value of the firm itself? Analyzes the effect of celebrity endorsement on sustainable firm value in the Korean telecommunications industry.
pubs.ssci-2019-03: Neighborhoods where people see more of each other may shop differently online. Analyzes how the degree of offline social interaction affects online shopping demand.
pubs.ssci-2019-04: What do consumers actually look at when buying a product with added features? Examines the role of design innovation in purchase behavior for augmented products.
pubs.ssci-2017-01: What brings customers back — money, or the people around them? Compares how social interaction and monetary incentives drive repeat consumer behavior.
pubs.ssci-2017-02: Installing a shopping app is not the same as buying through it. Separates app possession from mobile purchase to make sense of mobile shopping behavior.
pubs.ssci-2017-03: How niche products sell online is tied to the state of their brands offline. Links online niche sales to offline brand conditions.
pubs.ssci-2012-01: How are new customers won on the internet? Compares traditional and IS-enabled acquisition, laying groundwork for online customer acquisition strategy.
pubs.ssci-2012-02: What matters most in internet retailing? Distills the key drivers of online retail success for practicing managers.
pubs.ssci-2011-01: When your taste makes you a local minority, the internet matters more. Shows that ‘preference minorities’ — consumers underserved offline — lean harder on online shopping.
pubs.ssci-2010-01: Even online grocery shopping starts by following the neighbors. Analyzes the spatiotemporal pattern of imitation among new buyers at an online grocery retailer.
pubs.kci-2026-01: An influencer's word does not convert equally everywhere. Analyzes how the effect of influencer communication on purchase conversion varies with product type and regional characteristics.
pubs.kci-2026-02: When convenience stores and franchise supermarkets compete in the same trade area, private-brand goods face a different market. Analyzes how channel competition within a trade area affects PB sales performance.
pubs.kci-2026-03: A crisis at a franchise headquarters does not stay at headquarters. Analyzes how it ripples across the performance of the entire brand portfolio.
pubs.kci-2025-01: What makes someone install a food delivery app for the first time? Analyzes the role of social influence — what the people around us are using — in food delivery app adoption.
pubs.kci-2025-02: Why do luxury brands open stores in the metaverse? Examines how marketing in virtual spaces builds consumer engagement with luxury fashion brands.
pubs.kci-2024-01: For a virtual influencer, the face is the product. Analyzes how the facial characteristics of virtual influencers affect social media users' responses.
pubs.kci-2024-02: During the pandemic, some neighborhoods lost far more gyms than others. Shows that exposure to infection risk and compensatory spending had distinct effects on regional gym closures.
pubs.kci-2023-01: Is fandom driven by winning or by talking? Analyzes how a club's match results and social media activity affect fan engagement, and how fan tokens change that relationship.
pubs.kci-2023-02: Is being physically close to other firms really an advantage? Uses machine learning to unpack the role of industrial similarity and revisit assumptions about proximity.
pubs.kci-2023-03: What makes an unfamiliar food product trustworthy online? Analyzes how trust-building product strategies turn into word of mouth on online food platforms.
pubs.kci-2023-04: Trying a chatbot once is easy; coming back is not. Analyzes what determines continuance intention for chatbot services.
pubs.kci-2023-05: Can a single new app shake an entire market? Analyzes how one app launch reshapes the existing app ecosystem in digital healthcare.
pubs.kci-2023-06: What decides the finger that hits ‘skip ad’? Analyzes how video genre, viewers' digital-native traits, and media attributes affect pre-roll ad avoidance.
pubs.kci-2022-01: Short-form branded content works only if it is placed right. Shows that a sense of belonging mediates the path from short-form branded content to consumer response.
pubs.kci-2022-02: When a webtoon becomes a drama, news coverage does part of the marketing. Analyzes the effect of news publicity on viewers' online word of mouth for webtoon-based dramas.
pubs.kci-2022-03: When lockdowns lift, people do not simply pick up where they left off. Uses a Bayesian multilevel difference-in-differences design to measure how repealing lockdown changed socialization.
pubs.kci-2022-04: Does easier payment mean more shopping? Uses the cases of KakaoPay and Kakao Gift to analyze how adopting simple payment affects shopping app use.
pubs.kci-2022-05: Communities stay alive because someone runs them. Analyzes university ‘Bamboo Forest’ communities to derive management strategies that raise user participation.
pubs.kci-2022-06: The same ad can perform differently on a PC and on a phone. Compares the effectiveness of food ad targeting on video platforms across devices.
pubs.kci-2022-07: Who considered leaving their job during the pandemic? Analyzes online job search behavior during COVID-19 to identify what drove people to start looking.
pubs.kci-2021-01: Buzz on social media does not always turn into use. Uses time-series data on Seoul's bike-sharing service to analyze the link between social media and consumer decisions.
pubs.kci-2021-02: In an era of remote work and distancing, job satisfaction rested on new things. Analyzes what determined job satisfaction and mobile-based productivity during COVID-19.
pubs.kci-2020-01: How did a small craft brewery break into the market? Traces the growth strategy of a craft brewery startup through the case of Amazing Brewing Company.
pubs.kci-2020-02: For health foods, the name may be half the battle. Analyzes how product naming, customer experience, and firm promotions each affect health food purchases.
pubs.kci-2020-03: Hot, humid days send shoppers to different stores. Analyzes how weather discomfort and personal shopping preferences shape retail store choice.
pubs.kci-2018-01: The same luxury item performs differently depending on where it is sold. Shows that the effects of product, customer, and assortment on luxury sales vary by store type.
pubs.kci-2016-01: The words firms write and the words consumers leave behind both hold clues to sales. Analyzes online text data to derive strategies for growing revenue.
pubs.kci-2016-02: Marketing matters in business-to-business markets too. Analyzes how B2B firms' marketing activity and their customers' market environments affect sales performance.
pubs.kci-2015-01: When local stores disappear, niche products may find their buyers online. Analyzes how changes in the offline environment affect online demand for niche products.
pubs.kci-2015-02: What makes people pay for video on a phone? Verifies, with real data, the factors that drive mobile VOD content purchases.
pubs.kci-2014-01: How far has social media research come? A review mapping the trends and the gaps across social media research in the social sciences.
pubs.kci-2014-02: An online mall that leans on a portal can only grow so far. Analyzes how resource dependence on internet portals affects the growth of online shopping mall firms.
pubs.kci-2013-01: What sets apart the platforms where creators stay active? Shows that producer participation on user-generated content platforms affects consumer choice and engagement in distinct ways.
pubs.kci-2026-04: Do sneakers made from recycled materials fetch a premium on the resale market? Uses the case of Asics to analyze how price premiums form for products made with eco-friendly materials.
pubs.kci-2023-07: When workplace stress builds, is the phone a remedy or another burden? Analyzes the moderating role of mobile app use between workplace stressors and positive affect.
pubs.kci-2016-03: How do teenagers themselves see game regulation? Examines online game regulation from the perspective of those it targets, focusing on reactance and peer culture.
pubs.kci-2016-04: The same brand posts different numbers online and offline depending on the region. Analyzes how regional specificity creates gaps between offline and online channel performance.
pubs.kci-2016-05: What sets a high-performing store apart? Analyzes how in-store and surrounding conditions, together with the local market, affect store performance.
pubs.kci-2016-06: In-game currency or real cash — players choose differently. Analyzes game money and cash spending through experience, achievement, and regional disparity.
pubs.kci-2015-03: Moving to a new region can change the brands people buy online. Analyzes how consumers' regional migration affects shifts in online brand preference.
pubs.kci-2015-04: New and existing products post different numbers depending on the channel. Analyzes time-series data on experience goods to compare sales performance offline and online.
pubs.kci-2014-03: New players and long-time players leave a game for different reasons. Analyzes churn drivers among online game customers by customer type.
